name: Pigeon Pea
harvestProduct: dry grain (also green immature seed, and used as fodder/green manure)

evidence.quote: Pigeon peas are drought tolerant but are frost intolerant legume crops.
evidence.doc: Pigeon peas, DAFF (Lowveld Research Unit, Mpumalanga)

evidence.quote: Pigeon peas are best established by direct seeding in a well-prepared seedbed.
evidence.doc: Pigeon peas, DAFF (Lowveld Research Unit, Mpumalanga)

evidence.quote: Planting starts from October to December
evidence.doc: Pigeon peas, DAFF (Lowveld Research Unit, Mpumalanga)

daysToHarvestRange.notes: Source distinguishes 'long and medium duration' plants and notes early maturity under low rainfall, but gives no numeric days-to-maturity figure.

evidence.quote: The long and medium duration plants are planted at an interspacing of 70 to 90 cm.
evidence.doc: Pigeon peas, DAFF (Lowveld Research Unit, Mpumalanga)

rowSpacingRangeCm.notes: Source calls this 'interspacing' without clarifying whether it is row-to-row or plant-to-plant; treated here as row spacing since no separate in-row figure is given.

evidence.quote: placement of the seeds is from 4 to 5 cm deep; the deeper figure being in hand dibbling
evidence.doc: Pigeon peas, DAFF (Lowveld Research Unit, Mpumalanga)

evidence.quote: Seeds can be spread at a seed rate of 45 to 67 kg/ha
evidence.doc: Pigeon peas, DAFF (Lowveld Research Unit, Mpumalanga)

evidence.quote: The root nodules of the peas enrich the soil by adding about 40 kg of nitrogen per hectare.
evidence.doc: Pigeon peas, DAFF (Lowveld Research Unit, Mpumalanga)

zoneNotes.lowveld-bushveld: Named production districts: Limpopo (Bohlabela, Capricorn, Mopani) and Mpumalanga (Gert Sibande, Ekangala, Ehlanzeni South and North) -- all Lowveld/warm-interior districts, consistent with the crop's frost intolerance.
zoneNotes.highveld: Not addressed by the source; given the crop is stated to be frost intolerant, hard-frost highveld areas are likely unsuitable for a full-season crop (inference, not stated -- gap).

gaps: No numeric days-to-maturity figure; only a qualitative 'long vs medium duration' distinction and a note that low-rainfall conditions bring earlier maturity.
No yield figure (t/ha) anywhere in the source.
'Interspacing' of 70-90cm is not clearly labelled as row spacing vs in-row spacing, so in-row spacing is recorded as a gap rather than guessed.
No named varieties/cultivars -- only the generic 'long' and 'medium' duration plant types are mentioned.
Source's Oct-Dec planting window and production districts are all Lowveld (frost-free); no separate guidance for highveld, Western Cape, or coastal mild-frost areas.
summary: This DAFF/ARC Lowveld Research Unit brochure gives solid figures for sowing depth, seed rate, row spacing and nitrogen fixation (40 kg N/ha), and clearly documents frost intolerance and direct-seeding. It has no days-to-maturity or yield figures and no named varieties, so verdict is partial.
